`abhyasa.contract` holds the names that abhyasa and Leela share. It
imports only the standard library.

## Write an exercise

An exercise asks the learner to write one function. Its tests are plain
`assert` lines on that function.

``` python
from abhyasa.contract import check_exercise, safe_test, validate_nb_spec, handoff, read_handoff
ex = dict(task='Write rrf(ranks, k) that gives the reciprocal rank fusion score of a list of ranks.', fname='rrf',
          stub='def rrf(ranks, k=60): ...',
          tests=['assert rrf([1], 60) == 1/61',
                 dict(test='assert rrf([], 60) == 0', say='No ranks give zero.', hidden=True)])
assert check_exercise(ex)['fname'] == 'rrf'
assert not safe_test('assert rrf.__class__', 'rrf')
```

`check_exercise(ex)` gives the clean exercise, or raises `ValueError`
with the reason. It refuses an exercise that breaks one of these rules:

- `task` is a text that is not empty. `stub` is a text.
- `fname` is a plain Python name that does not start with `_`.
- `tests` has 1 to 12 items. An item is a test text, or an object
  `{test, say, hidden}`.
- Each test is one `assert` (`safe_test`). It uses only `fname`,
  literals, the names of its own comprehensions and the builtins in
  `SAFE_NAMES`. It has no import, no assignment, no `def`, no `lambda`
  and no attribute that starts with `_`. A string in it has at most 2000
  characters.

In Leela, the `add_exercise` tool puts an exercise in a lesson notebook.
It runs the solution only to check the tests, and it never stores the
solution. Leela’s `check_exercise` tool runs the learner’s cell and its
tests. It is a different function from
`abhyasa.contract.check_exercise`.

## The notebook spec of a walk step

A step that teaches with code opens in Leela as a notebook.
`validate_nb_spec(spec)` checks its spec and gives it back with only the
keys of the contract (`NB_KEYS`). A `ValueError` starts with the key
that fails.

``` python
nb = validate_nb_spec(dict(task=ex['task'], fname='rrf', stub=ex['stub'],
                           tests=[dict(test='assert rrf([1], 60) == 1/61', say='One list at rank 1.', shown=True)],
                           run=dict(say='fuse two ranked lists and print the top 3', minutes=2, makes='a ranked list',
                                    predict='Which item comes first?')))
assert nb['run']['say'] == 'Write the run here: fuse two ranked lists and print the top 3'
```

- `tests` is a list of objects `{test, say, shown}`. `say` is one line
  of 1 to 200 characters, and `shown` is true or false.
- `requires` has at most 5 package names. `data` has at most 8 entries
  `{name, path, what, need}`. A `name` is an upper-case Python name, and
  a `path` is inside the home folder, or empty for a folder that the
  learner adds.
- `run` is required: `say`,
  [`minutes`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#minutes)
  from 0 to 600, `makes` and `predict`. `say` starts with `RUN_SAY`, and
  the function adds it when it is missing.
- `demo` is the slug of a demo, at most 100 characters on one line, or
  empty.
- `task` and `stub` have no line that starts with `#|`. Each other text
  is one line.

## Open in Leela

`handoff` gives the path and query that Leela opens for a walk, a step,
a topic or a notebook in the vault. `read_handoff` reads them back and
checks them. It raises `ValueError` with the reason when the query is
not valid.

``` python
link = handoff('rrf-basics', 2)
assert link == '/learn?walk=rrf-basics&step=2'
assert read_handoff(link.split('?', 1)[1])['step'] == 2
```

abhyasa runs no code. It never calls Leela. A running Leela writes a
file that abhyasa reads, and abhyasa links only to an address on this
computer.

## Drive abhyasa from a host agent

`abhyasa.agent_tools` holds the learning operations that a host agent,
such as Leela, wraps as tools. Its import loads the whole engine and the
settings.

Each operation takes the learner’s store `lr` (a
[`Learning`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learning)).
An operation that calls a model also takes the host’s
`ask(prompt, sp='')`. Only
[`create_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#create_walk),
[`record_attempt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#record_attempt)
and
[`change_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#change_walk)
call a model.

<table>

<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>operation</th>
<th>what it does</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>create_walk(lr, ask, goal)</code></td>
<td>plans a walk to <code>goal</code> and saves it, with a passage from
the vault for each step</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>walk_state(lr, jid)</code></td>
<td>gives the walk as plain data: its steps, their quotes and checks,
and the gauge of each concept</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>record_attempt(lr, jid, i, answer, attempt_id, ask)</code></td>
<td>grades the answer to the check of step <code>i</code> and saves it,
once for each <code>attempt_id</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>record_code_attempt(lr, jid, i, ok, attempt_id)</code></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>note_confusion(lr, jid, i, note)</code></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>change_walk(lr, ask, jid, instruction)</code></td>
<td>changes the walk from the learner’s words</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><a

<a

<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#move_idea"><code>move_idea</code></a></td>
<td>locks, removes or moves one idea</td>
</tr>

<td><code>add_source(lr, jid, source)</code></td>

</tr>
<tr>

<a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#restore_version"><code>restore_version</code></a></td>
<td>lists the earlier versions of a walk; goes back to one</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>explain_here(lr, jid, i, note)</code></td>
<td>gives the data and the rules to explain step <code>i</code>; the
agent writes the explanation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>learner_context(lr, jid, i)</code></td>
<td>gives a short plain-text block for a system prompt</td>
</tr>

Each operation gives one dict with `status` (`ok`, `error` or
`stopped`), `operation_id`, `vault`, `walk`, `step`, `revision`, `data`
and `error`. An expected failure does not raise. It has `status`
`error`, an `error` from `ERRORS`, and `data['message']`. A change to a
walk takes the `revision` that the caller last saw, and refuses an old
one with `stale_state`. Each change has an Undo in the history of the
walk. `TOOLS` lists each operation that a host makes a tool, with the
arguments that the model gives. `READS` names the tools that change
nothing. The host owns privacy:
[`create_walk`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#create_walk)
takes the host’s `guard(text)`.

## The tutor in Python

This example runs offline.
[`temp_learning`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#temp_learning)
makes a shelf in a vault in a temporary folder, and
[`Fake`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/models.html#fake) takes
the place of the model.

``` python
from abhyasa.learner import temp_learning
from abhyasa.models import Fake
from abhyasa.tutor import Tutor
lr = temp_learning()
lr.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
fake = Fake({'You grade one answer': dict(correct=True, grade=8, first_error='', misconception='', feedback='Yes. Only the order counts.')},
            dflt=dict(question='Why can you compare ranks from two systems, but not their scores?', answer='Ranks share one scale.',
                      rubric=['ranks share one scale']))
t = Tutor(lr, fake, context=False)
q = t.next()
r = t.answer(q.id, 'A rank is a position, and positions use the same scale in each list.', confidence=80)
assert r.outcome == 'solid'
```

- In a notebook, `from abhyasa.tutor import learn` and
  `learn('reciprocal-rank-fusion')` give a question card on the default
  vault.
- A test never opens the real vault (`~/.vishalakshi/vault.db`). Use
  [`temp_learning()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#temp_learning).
  Set `ABHYASA_CONFIG` to a temporary folder and `RAMABANA_CONFIG` to a
  `config.toml` file in a temporary folder, so that the test reads no
  real settings.
- abhyasa makes demos with rupaka. Read the `rupaka` skill to write one.
  `abhyasa.show.make_demo(lr, ask, slug)` makes a demo for a concept and
  stores it, or gives None when the model fails. It plays the demo in a
  browser only when
  [`rupaka.check.can_check()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/rupaka/check.html#can_check)
  is True. `make_explainer(lr, ask, slug)` makes a 3D explainer.

## The app

`uv run abhyasa` in a clone, or `abhyasa` after
`uv tool install abhyasa`, starts the web app on http://127.0.0.1:5077.
It answers only requests from this computer. `ABHYASA_VAULT` sets the
vault file, and `ABHYASA_CONFIG` sets the folder of the settings and
keys.

## This sheet in a harness

The `pyskills` entry point `abhyasa` names this module. Leela and
ramabana list it with the other skills, and `read_skill('abhyasa')`
reads it. When `pyskills` is installed, this module allows the names in
`ALLOW` in a sandbox. They are the checks of `abhyasa.contract`, which
read no file of the learner and need no model.

`mv_skill_md(dry_run=False)` writes this sheet as
`.agents/skills/abhyasa/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/abhyasa/SKILL.md`
in the current git repository, for Claude Code, Codex and other
harnesses that read Agent Skills.

## The hook

The Markdown cells above are the docstring of `abhyasa.skill`.
`pyskills` reads the docstring without an import, and takes its first
paragraph as the summary. A skill loader that imports the module pays
only for `abhyasa.contract`.

`ALLOW` lists the functions that a sandboxed agent may call. `pyskills`
is not a direct dependency of abhyasa, so the hook runs only when it is
installed.

## The SKILL.md

[`skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/skill.html#skill_md)
gives the same text as an Agent Skills `SKILL.md`: a front matter with
`name` and `description`, then the body. The description is a JSON
string, which YAML reads as a quoted text, so a colon in it is safe.

## Tests

Each name in `ALLOW` is a real function. `allow` skips a missing name
and says nothing, so this test catches a rename.

``` python
from abhyasa.skill import ALLOW
for m, ns in ALLOW.items():
    for n in ns: assert callable(getattr(m, n, None)), f'{m.__name__}.{n}'
```

The contract examples of the sheet run.

``` python
ns = {}
import abhyasa.skill as sk
for ex in sk.__doc__.split('```python\n')[1:4]: exec(ex.split('```', 1)[0], ns)
assert ns['nb']['fname'] == 'rrf' and ns['link'].startswith('/learn?')
```

The front matter has the name and a one-line description. The `SKILL.md`
copies in this repository match the sheet. After an edit to the sheet,
run `mv_skill_md(dry_run=False)` and commit the copies.

``` python
md_text = sk.skill_md()
head, body = md_text.split('\n---\n', 1)
assert head.startswith('---\nname: abhyasa\ndescription: "Work with abhyasa')
assert body.lstrip().startswith('## Words')
for d in ('.agents', '.claude'): test_eq((Path('..')/d/'skills/abhyasa/SKILL.md').read_text(), md_text)
```
